examples.ko: 정치에 환멸을 느껴서 뉴스를 안 봐요.
examples.en: I'm disillusioned with politics, so I don't watch the news.
After long expectations, only disillusionment was left.

examples.ko: 직장 생활에 환멸이 와서 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: I've become disenchanted with work life and want to take a break.
I quit that job because of my disillusionment.
The gap between ideal and reality led to disillusionment.
As my disillusionment deepened, my motivation vanished too.

explain: '실망'보다 강해서, 믿고 기대했던 사람, 제도, 일에 정이 떨어질 만큼 실망했을 때 써요. '환멸을 느끼다'가 가장 기본이 되는 짝이에요. '환멸감'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 일 이후로 친구에게 환멸감이 들었어요.
phrases.en: After that incident, I felt disillusioned with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환멸'과 같은 뜻으로, 느낌을 강조하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 환멸, stressing the feeling.

phrases.en: I became disillusioned with people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환멸을 느끼다'와 비슷하게 마음에 환멸이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 환멸을 느끼다, used when disillusionment arises in one's mind.

phrases.en: I was very disappointed with the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환멸보다 약한 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier expression that is weaker than 환멸.

explain_en: It is stronger than '실망' and is used when you were so let down by a person, system or job you trusted that you lose all affection for it. '환멸을 느끼다' is the most basic pairing. It can also be said as '환멸감'.

examples.en: That son is deeply devoted to his parents.
A devoted daughter takes care of her parents.
Grandmother was moved by her grandson's devotion.
He is known for his devotion to his parents.

examples.ko: 효성은 말이 아니라 행동으로 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: Filial devotion should be shown by actions, not words.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에는 효성이 큰 아이가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Old tales often feature a child with great filial devotion.

explain: '효도'가 부모님께 하는 행동이라면 '효성'은 부모를 위하는 마음이에요. '효성이 지극하다', '효성이 깊다'처럼 마음의 크기를 말할 때 써요. 말투가 조금 옛날 같아서 요즘은 '효도'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The daughter did her utmost out of devotion to her parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 다해서 부모님을 위한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to give one's whole heart in caring for one's parents.
phrases.en_equiv: to be fully devoted to one's parents

phrases.en: The devoted daughter calls her parents every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모를 위하는 마음이 큰 사람이나 행동을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person or action that shows great care for parents.

phrases.en: He is well known in the neighborhood as a dutiful son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 효성이 깊은 아들을 말하고, 딸은 '효녀'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A son who is devoted to his parents; for a daughter, say '효녀'.

explain_en: Devotion to one's parents — filial piety, fairly formal/literary. If 효도 is what you do for your parents, 효성 is the heart behind it. It is used to describe how strong that feeling is, as in 효성이 지극하다 or 효성이 깊다. It sounds a little old-fashioned, so people today use 효도 more.

examples.ko: 아이는 엄마를 보자 흑흑 울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The child started sobbing as soon as she saw her mother.

examples.ko: 방에서 누가 흑흑 소리 내며 울고 있어요.
examples.en: Someone in the room is crying with sobs.
My friend sobbed, saying she failed the exam.
Sob, sob, my beloved puppy is gone!

examples.ko: 드라마를 보다가 나도 모르게 흑흑 울었어요.
examples.en: While watching a drama, I found myself sobbing.

examples.ko: 그는 한참을 흑흑 흐느끼다가 겨우 말을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: He sobbed for a long while before he could finally speak.

explain: 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 크게 우는 '엉엉'과 달리 숨을 삼키듯 작게 우는 느낌이고, 채팅에서는 슬픈 척 장난스럽게 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I cried and sobbed while watching the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '울다' 앞에 붙여 작게 숨을 삼키며 우는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before 'cry' to describe crying quietly with caught breath.

phrases.example: 아이가 흑흑 소리를 내며 방에 들어갔어요.
phrases.en: The child went into the room making sobbing sounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우는 소리를 직접 흉내 내어 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression that directly imitates the sound of crying.

phrases.example: 채팅에서 친구가 '숙제가 너무 많아요, 슬퍼요 흑흑'이라고 썼어요.
phrases.en: In the chat, my friend wrote, 'There's so much homework, I'm sad, boohoo.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 채팅에서 슬픈 척 장난스럽게 문장 끝에 덧붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful add-on at the end of a sentence in chats, pretending to be sad.

explain_en: It imitates the sound of crying. Unlike '엉엉', which is loud crying, it feels like quiet sobbing with held breath, and in chats people also use it jokingly to act sad.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에서 주인이 몽둥이를 들고 도둑을 쫓아요.
examples.en: In the old tale, the owner chases the thief with a club.
The child picked up a branch as thick as a club.
You must never hit people with a club.
A thick club is lying by the road.

examples.ko: 개를 쫓으려고 집어 든 몽둥이는 너무 무거웠어요.
examples.en: The club I picked up to drive the dog away was too heavy.
The police stopped the person holding a club.

explain: 몽둥이는 사람이나 동물을 때리는 굵고 긴 막대라서 폭력의 느낌이 강해요. 야구에서 치는 막대는 '방망이'라고 하고, '야구 몽둥이'라고 하면 어색해요. '도깨비 방망이'도 몽둥이처럼 생겼지만 '방망이'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: In the old tale, the owner hits the thief with a club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몽둥이는 때리는 도구라서 이 짝말이 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since a 몽둥이 is for hitting, this pairing is the most common.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 몽둥이를 들고 서 있었어요.
phrases.en: The man was standing holding a club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위협하는 장면에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in threatening scenes.

phrases.example: 굵은 몽둥이가 문 옆에 놓여 있어요.
phrases.en: A thick club is lying next to the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몽둥이의 모양을 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of a club.

explain_en: Thick stick, used for hitting or driving off. A 몽둥이 is a thick, long stick used for hitting, so it feels violent. The bat in baseball is a '방망이', and '야구 몽둥이' sounds odd. The goblin's magic club is also called '도깨비 방망이'.

t90.ax: A thick club is lying by the road.

en: to be stiff; to be dry and sticky

examples.ko: 인공 눈물을 넣었더니 눈이 덜 뻑뻑해요.
examples.en: After I put in artificial tears, my eyes feel less dry and stiff.
The door is stiff, so it doesn't open easily.

examples.ko: 밥이 너무 뻑뻑해서 물을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: The rice was too thick and dry, so I added more water.

examples.ko: 자전거 체인이 뻑뻑하면 기름을 쳐야 해요.
examples.en: If the bicycle chain is stiff, you need to oil it.
If the dough is too thick, add a little water.
The drawer was sticking. Could you take a look at it?

explain: 물기나 기름기가 적어서 잘 움직이지 않거나 잘 풀어지지 않는 느낌이에요. 문, 서랍, 반죽, 눈 모두에 써요. 반대 느낌은 '부드럽다'로 말하면 돼요.

phrases.en: The dough was stiff, so I added more water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뻑뻑하다'의 활용형으로, 물기가 적어 되직한 음식에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form also used for food that is thick and low in moisture.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 화면을 봤더니 눈이 뻑뻑해요.
phrases.en: My eyes feel dry and stiff after looking at a screen all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 물기가 없어서 깜빡이기 불편한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The feeling that eyes are too dry to blink comfortably.

phrases.en: I oiled the door, so it isn't stiff anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 잘 움직인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning it moves smoothly.

explain_en: Parts that move poorly from friction or dryness (문), or dry eyes. It describes something that doesn't move or loosen easily because it lacks moisture or oil. It works for doors, drawers, dough and eyes alike. For the opposite feeling, you can say '부드럽다'.

t90.ax: The door is stiff, so it doesn't open easily.

examples.en: I washed my hands at the sink.
The water in the sink isn't draining well.
There's no soap at the bathroom sink.

examples.ko: 칫솔은 세면대 옆 컵에 꽂아 두세요.
examples.en: Put the toothbrush in the cup next to the sink.
The hotel sink was so small that it was inconvenient.
I bought baking soda to clean the sink.

explain: 한국 집에서는 '세면대'에서 손을 씻고 세수와 양치를 해요. 샤워는 '샤워기' 아래에서 하고, 부엌에서 설거지하는 곳은 '싱크대'예요. 세면대와 싱크대를 서로 바꿔 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I wash my face at the sink every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세면대를 쓰는 가장 흔한 일상 장면이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday use of a washbasin.
phrases.en_equiv: to wash one's face at the sink

phrases.en: The bathroom sink is clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세면대가 있는 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where the washbasin is.

phrases.en: The sink is clogged, so the water won't drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 안 내려갈 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when water won't drain.

explain_en: Sink in a bathroom for washing face and hands. In a Korean home you wash your hands, face, and brush your teeth at the '세면대'. Showers happen under the '샤워기', and the kitchen place for dishes is the '싱크대'. The two words are not swapped.

examples.en: It was cold, so I pulled the edge of the blanket up to my chin.

examples.ko: 아이가 자는 사이에 이불자락이 바닥으로 흘러내렸어요.
examples.en: While the child slept, the edge of the blanket slipped down to the floor.

examples.ko: 이불자락 끝을 꼭 잡고 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: I fell asleep holding the end of the blanket tightly.

examples.ko: 엄마가 이불자락을 살짝 들추고 방에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: Mom lifted the corner of the blanket slightly and came into the room.

examples.ko: 이불자락에 커피를 쏟아서 빨래를 해야 해요.
examples.en: I spilled coffee on the edge of the comforter, so I have to wash it.

examples.ko: 고양이가 이불자락 속으로 쏙 들어가 버렸어요.
examples.en: The cat slipped right under the edge of the blanket.

explain: '치맛자락', '옷자락'처럼 '-자락'이 붙은 말과 같은 계열이에요. 이불을 끌어올리거나 들추거나 붙잡는 동작과 함께 자주 나와요. 이불 전체는 '이불을 덮다/걷어차다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: A cold wind blew, so I pulled the blanket up to my shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추울 때 이불을 위로 당기는 동작에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for pulling a blanket up when cold.
phrases.en_equiv: to pull up the blanket edge

phrases.example: 무서운 영화를 보며 이불자락을 꽉 붙잡았어요.
phrases.en: I gripped the blanket tightly while watching a scary movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긴장하거나 무서울 때의 행동을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows a nervous or scared reaction.

phrases.en: Mom lifted the edge of the blanket and woke the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이불 끝을 살짝 들어 올리는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lifting the edge of the blanket slightly.

explain_en: It belongs to the same family as '치맛자락' and '옷자락', which also use '-자락'. It often appears with actions like pulling up, lifting, or gripping the blanket. For the whole blanket, you say things like '이불을 덮다' or '이불을 걷어차다'.

examples.en: A scrap of paper turned up in the drawer.
I made doll clothes from scraps of cloth.
A phone number is written on that scrap.
Even a crumb of bread is fine; please give me anything.
Be careful when you clear away the pieces of the broken plate.

examples.ko: 이런 쪼가리 하나 때문에 싸우지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't fight over a little scrap like this.

explain: '조각'을 낮춰서 편하게 부르는 말이에요. 종이, 천, 빵처럼 작고 보잘것없는 조각에 써요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 '조각'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: A scrap of paper came out of my pocket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이고, 쓸모없어 보이는 종이를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for a worthless-looking scrap of paper.

phrases.en: I wiped the cup with a scrap of cloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 낡은 천 조각을 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual name for a small, worn piece of cloth.

phrases.en: I ate a piece of bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쪼가리'보다 격식 있고 어디서나 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral than '쪼가리' and usable anywhere.

explain_en: It is a casual, slightly dismissive way to say '조각' (piece). It is used for small, humble bits of paper, cloth, bread and so on. In formal settings, say '조각'.

t90.ax: A phone number is written on that scrap.

en: to crush; to squash; to dent

examples.en: I accidentally stepped on the can and crushed it.
Be careful not to squash the box.
The child squashes the paper cup with his hand.
I almost dented the car next to me while parking.

examples.ko: 화가 난 그는 종이를 찌그러뜨려 던졌어요.
examples.en: Angry, he crumpled the paper and threw it.
If you squash the hat, it won't go back into shape.

explain: '찌그러지다'는 저절로 모양이 망가지는 것이고, '찌그러뜨리다'는 누군가 힘을 가해 그렇게 만드는 거예요. '찌그러트리다'로도 쓸 수 있어요. 캔이나 상자처럼 단단한 물건에 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I crushed the paper cup with my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '찌그러뜨리다'와 뜻이 같고, '-트리다'로 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning; '-트리다' is an accepted alternative spelling.

phrases.en: I pressed the empty plastic bottle down hard and crushed it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 주어 누르는 모습을 더해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the sense of pressing down with force.

phrases.en: Please don't crush the delivery box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request or warning not to crush something.

explain_en: Transitive, you deliberately dent something like a can (캔을 찌그러뜨리다) '찌그러지다' means something loses its shape by itself, while '찌그러뜨리다' means someone applies force to make that happen. '찌그러트리다' is also an accepted form. It is often used for fairly hard objects such as cans and boxes.

t90.ax: Be careful not to squash the box.

examples.en: I carefully cut out the potato sprouts with the tip of the knife.
The tip of this knife is sharp, so be careful.

examples.ko: 요리사는 칼끝을 살짝 세워 칼집을 냈어요.
examples.en: The chef tilted the tip of the knife slightly and scored the food.
Be careful that your hand doesn't touch the knife tip.

examples.ko: 칼끝을 아래로 향하게 두고 건네지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't hand it over with the tip pointing down.
I cut the packing tape gently with the knife tip.

explain: 칼의 뾰족한 끝부분이에요. 칼의 다른 부분은 날 쪽이 '칼날', 뒤쪽이 '칼등', 손잡이가 '칼자루'예요. '붓끝', '펜 끝'처럼 '-끝'이 붙는 말과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The tip of this knife is pointy, so it's dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칼의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of a knife.

phrases.en: I dug out the potato eyes with the tip of the knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '-으로'를 붙여 칼의 어느 부분을 쓰는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -으로 shows which part of the knife is used.
phrases.en_equiv: with the tip of the knife

phrases.en: Be careful of the knife tip when cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used when talking about safety.
phrases.en_equiv: to watch out for the knife tip

explain_en: It is the pointed end of a knife. Other parts are '칼날' (blade edge), '칼등' (back of the blade) and '칼자루' (handle). It helps to learn it alongside words ending in '-끝', such as '붓끝' (brush tip).

examples.en: A small weed grew in a crack of the building.

examples.ko: 사람들 틈바구니에 끼어서 움직일 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: I was stuck among the crowd and couldn't move.

examples.ko: 강대국들 틈바구니에서 작은 나라는 살아남기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Squeezed between great powers, the small country struggled to survive.
A coin fell into the gap of the sofa.

examples.ko: 빡빡한 일정 틈바구니에 잠깐 쉴 시간을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a little time to rest in the gaps of a tight schedule.
Wind comes in through the gap, so the room is cold.

explain: 그냥 '틈'보다 좁은 사이에 끼어 있는 느낌이 강해요. 물건 사이뿐 아니라 사람, 나라, 일정 사이에 끼인 상황에도 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '틈새'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Wind comes in through the gap in the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '틈바구니'와 비슷하지만 좁게 벌어진 자리 자체를 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 틈바구니, but more often used for the narrow opening itself.

phrases.en: A small flower bloomed in a crevice in the rock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단한 물건 사이의 좁은 틈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a narrow crevice between hard objects.

phrases.en: The small country survived squeezed between great powers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘센 나라들 사이에 끼인 어려운 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a difficult situation of being caught between powerful countries.

explain_en: It strongly feels like being caught in a narrow space, more than plain '틈'. It is used not only between objects but also for being stuck among people, countries or schedules. A similar word is '틈새'.

examples.ko: 쌀 한 포대를 사서 집에 가져왔어요.
examples.en: I bought a sack of rice and brought it home.
I filled the sack with potatoes.
The cement sack is too heavy for me to lift.

examples.ko: 할머니가 고구마 한 포대를 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother sent me a sack of sweet potatoes.
I tied the sacks and stacked them in the warehouse.
The flour sack tore and the floor turned white.

explain: '한 포대, 두 포대'처럼 큰 자루를 세는 단위로도 많이 써요. '자루'는 크기에 상관없이 쓰고, 작은 것은 '봉지'라고 해요. '쌀 한 포대'처럼 무겁고 많은 양을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I loaded three sacks of sweet potatoes into the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: '포대'는 숫자 뒤에서 큰 자루를 세는 단위예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 포대 is a counter for big sacks, used after a number.

phrases.en: The rice sack is too heavy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌀이나 곡식이 든 큰 자루를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for big sacks of rice or grain.

phrases.en: I put the chestnuts in a sack.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자루'는 크기에 상관없이 쓰는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 자루 is a broader word that works for any size.

explain_en: It is also widely used as a counter for large sacks, as in '한 포대, 두 포대'. '자루' is used regardless of size, and small ones are '봉지'. It fits heavy, large amounts, as in '쌀 한 포대'.

examples.ko: 자동차 검사소가 우리 집 근처에 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new vehicle inspection station opened near my house.

examples.ko: 차를 끌고 검사소에 가서 정기 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: I drove to the inspection station and got my regular inspection.

examples.ko: 검사소 앞에 차가 길게 줄 서 있었어요.
examples.en: A long line of cars was waiting in front of the inspection station.
Please tell me where the nearest inspection station is.

examples.ko: 이 검사소는 예약하면 대기 시간이 짧아요.
examples.en: If you book ahead at this inspection station, the waiting time is short.

examples.ko: 검사소 직원이 서류를 확인하고 도장을 찍어 줬어요.
examples.en: The inspection station staff checked the documents and stamped them.

explain: 자동차, 농산물, 식품처럼 법에 따라 상태를 확인하는 곳이에요. 가장 흔한 예는 '자동차 검사소'예요. 앞에 검사하는 대상을 붙여서 어떤 검사소인지 말해요.

phrases.en: They check the quality at the agricultural product inspection station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 대상을 붙여 어떤 검사를 하는 곳인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The thing inspected goes first to say what kind of station it is.

phrases.example: 검사소 예약은 인터넷으로 할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can make an inspection reservation online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가기 전에 시간을 미리 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when setting a time before going.

phrases.en: I have to go to the inspection office tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사를 받으러 직접 가는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Talks about going in person to get inspected.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the inspection office

explain_en: It is a place that checks the condition of things like vehicles, farm products or food as required by law. The most common example is the '자동차 검사소'. The thing being inspected is put in front to say which kind it is.

examples.en: On autumn nights I can hear the chirping.

examples.ko: 귀뚜라미가 귀뚤귀뚤 울어서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The crickets are chirping, so I can't sleep.
A chirping sound started outside the window.
The yard of the country house is full of chirping.

examples.ko: 귀뚤귀뚤 우는 소리를 들으니 가을이 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: Hearing the chirping makes it feel like autumn has come.

examples.ko: 어디선가 귀뚤귀뚤 울던 소리가 갑자기 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The chirping from somewhere suddenly stopped.

explain: 귀뚜라미가 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이라서 가을 밤의 느낌과 함께 자주 나와요. 매미 소리는 '맴맴'처럼 곤충마다 소리를 흉내 내는 말이 달라요.

phrases.en: Every night a chirping sound comes from outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀뚜라미 소리가 들린다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a cricket's sound can be heard.

phrases.en: A chirping can be heard from the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 어디에서 들리는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where the sound is heard from.

phrases.example: 귀뚜라미 울음소리를 들으니 가을이 왔구나 싶어요.
phrases.en: Hearing the crickets chirp makes me think autumn has come.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의성어가 아니라 명사로 소리를 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the sound with a noun rather than an onomatopoeia.

explain_en: It imitates the sound of a cricket, so it often appears with the feeling of an autumn night. Each insect has its own sound word, for example '맴맴' for a cicada.
